//: Papercusp worker hooks as a Claude plugin (papercusp-worker-integration-2026-06-04, D-005). These reference the worker hook scripts at their stable installed location (~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/, populated by install-standalone-mcp.sh) — the plugin is a thin wiring convenience over the installed worker, NOT a standalone bundle (the scripts need a running operator + ~/.papercusp). All hooks self-gate on PAPERCUSP_SID + fail open. The activity-report hook is the cross-CLI activity bridge. RTK output compression for Bash lives INSIDE pretooluse-restricted-egress-guard.mjs, the ONE Bash hook that returns updatedInput (WI-6554700010009291). Claude Code resolves several hooks that each return updatedInput by completion order, so the old separate inline `rtk hook claude` entry could race the guard and silently drop its network sandbox. The guard rewrites with RTK first, then sandboxes that form when the session is restricted, judges every deny on the original command, skips vitest commands (EI-9471: rtk's vitest parser once dropped a single-file filter and ran the full suite) and fails open when rtk is absent.

PreToolUse.//: EI-21971958067151594 — `capability:bash` is the SAME shell reached over MCP, and a native-only `Bash` matcher left it exempt from every deny in pretooluse-bash-resource-gate.sh (measured 2026-08-31: `tauri-agent-tools dom` was DENIED as Bash and RAN as capability:bash against a foreign webview; the self-matching-pgrep wait-loop likewise ran to its timeout). Deliberately a SEPARATE entry rather than widening the `Bash` matcher above: the egress guard there REWRITES the Bash payload, and capability:bash applies RTK server-side instead (capability/rtk-rewrite.ts) — the safety gate must gain coverage without dragging a rewriter along. Ordering is irrelevant here because this entry holds only the gate, and a deny wins regardless.
